messages:
ReleaseBot: :rotating_light: prod-canary deployment batch-20260315 started, health check failures detected on 3/6 canary pods. check logs: https://ci.redwood/release/982
PagerDuty: paging Priya (on-call) for prod-canary severity=high -> https://pagerduty.inc/PD-7331
Priya (on-call): on it. looking at console now, can someone paste `kubectl get pods -n prod -l release=batch-20260315 -o wide`?
Jordan (release-owner): I kicked the gradual rollout at 09:12 UTC. I see failed pod restarts in the canary group. not sure it's config vs binary.
Alex (sre): quick check: `kubectl get events -n prod | grep batch-20260315` shows repeated liveness probe failures, OOMKilled on one pod and SIGTERM on two others.
Lee (devex): weird, the image includes a new runtime change that adjusts worker concurrency. might interact with liveness threshold.
Priya (on-call): customer impact? any external 5xx spikes?
OpsBot: Metrics: prod-inference-frontend 5xx spike from baseline 0.3% -> 2.4% across cfg=traffic:canary for the last 7m. Latency p95 jumped 4x. (source: observability)
Jordan (release-owner): that's bad. Canary was 5% traffic. estimate ~1.8% of overall requests affected. will start mitigation.
Alex (sre): suggest flip feature flag `release_v3_canary` off for canary traffic first. command:
```
curl -X POST "https://flags.redwood/api/toggle" -d '{"flag":"release_v3_canary","state":false}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
Priya (on-call): toggled flag off at 09:22 UTC. confirm: featureflags shows `release_v3_canary=false`.
Jordan (release-owner): flag off confirmed. traffic should divert to previous model. monitoring...
OpsBot: After flag toggle, 5xxs decreased from 2.4% -> 1.6% in 90s but not back to baseline. Some pods still crash on start due to init container timing out.
Alex (sre): can you share `kubectl logs -n prod pod/batch-20260315-canary-2 -c app --tail=80`? I see an exception in startup sequence referencing `kv-cache` allocation.
Jordan (release-owner): logs:
```
2026-03-15T09:21:44Z ERROR service StartFailed: kv-cache allocation failed: "insufficient memory"
2026-03-15T09:21:44Z INFO process received SIGTERM
```
Lee (devex): that suggests our new concurrency default increases memory pressure at cold start. our liveness probe is aggressive (10s). container starts slower now -> probed as unhealthy -> kube kills it -> crashloop.
Priya (on-call): mitigation options: 1) widen liveness probe to 60s for canary pods, 2) rollback the deployment to previous revision, 3) increase node pool memory (slow). Recommend rollback to stop customer impact quickly.
Jordan (release-owner): agree. I'll initiate rollback to rollout revision v981.
Alex (sre): oncall, ensure a temporary traffic hold to prevent further canary routing while rollback proceeds.
Priya (on-call): pausing canary routing via router: `POST /api/router/pause?scope=canary` -> done at 09:28 UTC
Jordan (release-owner): running:
```
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/batch-api --to-revision=981
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/batch-api
```
OpsBot: rollout undo started at 09:29 UTC. Watching pods...
Alex (sre): detected one pod stuck Terminating due to finalizer on pvc; I'll remove orphan finalizer carefully: `kubectl patch pvc mycache -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":null}}'` (handed off to storage team if needed)
Lee (devex): storage finalizer cleared at 09:33 UTC, new pods coming up with old image.
OpsBot: new replica set stable at 09:36 UTC. health checks green. 5xxs down to 0.35% and p95 latency back to normal baseline.
Jordan (release-owner): rollback complete. blocking change is new concurrency default + liveness too aggressive. root cause hypothesis noted.
Priya (on-call): handing off to Jordan for postmortem and followups. Paging next SEV owner: Jordan. @Jordan please open incident ticket ENG-1234 with action items: revert default concurrency, add startup grace to liveness for next canary, add mem cap tests to CI.
Jordan (release-owner): ack. I'll draft the postmortem and include diff, repro steps, and customer impact estimate (~1.8% requests over ~15m window; transient errors).
Alex (sre): recommend adding an automated pre-flight that simulates cold-start memory for new images in staging.
Lee (devex): will add to backlog and PR for liveness tuning before next rollout.
Priya (on-call): incident severity reduced to SEV2 at 09:40 UTC, on-call handover complete. final note: notify support to message affected customers if we see any escalations. :white_check_mark:
OpsBot: incident thread closed for active mitigation at 09:41 UTC. Follow-up: retrospective due EOD tomorrow.
Jordan (release-owner): thanks everyone. I'll post the postmortem draft here when ready.
